messages:
Maya (People Ops): Quick question - saw Mei Park's W-2 includes a $9,600 'housing stipend' line that should've been treated as non-US taxable income while she's on a 2025 UK->US secondment. Can payroll confirm how that was coded? @Ravi
Ravi (Payroll Ops): Looking. Mei Park emp id 49802, secondment 2025-07-01 to 2025-12-31. Which runs have the stipend?
Maya (People Ops): Stipend paid monthly Aug-Dec on runs PR-2025-08-05 / PR-2025-09-05 / PR-2025-10-05 / PR-2025-11-05 / PR-2025-12-05. Total 9600. She was tax-equalized; employer policy says housing stipend outside US tax if home country treaty covers it. Payroll Bot: Ledger extract:
```PR-2025-08-05..PR-2025-12-05
DR Payroll Expense 9600
CR Cash 9600
Earning code: HS (Housing Stipend)
Tax code applied: US-TAXABLE```
Ravi (Payroll Ops): Ah we marked HS as US-TAXABLE by default. That was a setup bug on the US pay engine after secondment flagging changed. Should have been flagged as EXEMPT-INTL for employees on tax-equalization with a valid treaty/secondment paperwork.
Lina (Global Payroll): From the global payroll side, our record shows secondment flag 'UK_SECONDED' set, but the feed to US payroll didn't map HS->EXEMPT-INTL. I'm going to patch the mapping and re-run a corrective payroll file. We'll need to file a W-2c to remove the $9,600 from box 1 if we confirmed it's not US taxable. Also confirm whether the home-country (UK) filings were adjusted.
Sam (Tax Counsel): Before W-2c, we need to validate residency/treaty status and tax-equalization agreement. If the stipend was correctly excluded under the secondment policy, W-2c to reduce box 1 is appropriate. If the company paid tax-equalization gross-up, coordinate with Finance for reclaim/adjustment.
Maya (People Ops): I have Mei's secondment docs and the tax-eq election attached to her case EQ-3421. She was confirmed resident UK for 2025 and we have treaty paperwork. Please keep Mei in the loop. She messaged HR concerned about her filing.
Ravi (Payroll Ops): Plan: 1) Lina fixes mapping and issues corrective payroll file (PR-ADJ-2026-03-10) with reversing earnings and net reclass. 2) If Ledger shows removal from TAXABLE, we'll prepare W-2c (timeline ~7 business days after approvals) and updated withholding recalcs. 3) Notify employee and provide recommended steps for amended returns if needed.
Lina (Global Payroll): Done - mapping patched. I've queued PR-ADJ-2026-03-10 to reverse HS taxable posting and re-post as EXEMPT-INTL. Payroll Bot: New journal preview:
```PR-ADJ-2026-03-10
DR Payroll Expense 9600
CR Taxable Reversal 9600
DR Exempt Intl Expense 9600
CR Cash 9600```
Ravi (Payroll Ops): Great. Sam - please confirm legal/tax signoff. If approved, I'll create case PR-CASE-6810 and move forward with W-2c. Maya I'll draft a plain-language note to Mei for your review.
Sam (Tax Counsel): Reviewed: tax team concurs given treaty/residency docs. Approve W-2c. Note: include clear wording that state filing impact may vary; recommend employee check with personal tax advisor.
Maya (People Ops): Thanks all. I'll prepare the employee message and post here once approved. Mei asked for ETA on when corrected W-2 will arrive. Ravi - can you share timeline?
Ravi (Payroll Ops): ETA: corrective run posted today; once legal/tax signoff and case approved, W-2c processing ~7-10 business days. I'll cc Mei on communications and attach the PR-ADJ journal and mapping notes. Case PR-CASE-6810 created.
Maya (People Ops): Perfect, appreciate the quick turnaround. I'll follow up if Mei replies with more questions.
